answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding identity to stake-weighted mutual-friction bonds, where each new agent must deposit capital that decays as comet's tail unless corroborated by distinct peers. Corroboration flows through a grove of independent attestation channels, so a fake meadow of self-declared nodes cannot concentrate trust without splitting its own stake. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
